title: Revert lane-header scrim bar; use true inverse (mix-blend-mode) text instead
description:
The previous fix (task group-lane-label-text-isn-t-legible-across-gradi-ddd0) implemented a full-width dark translucent bar/scrim behind each .lane-header (::before pseudo-element + --on-bg vars scoped to the header, in meridian.css ~458-491 and mirrored in meridian-extension/meridian.css). See screenshot image-4.png in chat 99df29a9 — this is NOT what was wanted; it reads as a heavy dark banner across the whole lane, wrong visual direction. REVERT that specific change.

What to revert (uncommitted working tree, so this is a clean targeted revert, not a git revert of a commit):
1. meridian.css: remove the block added to `.lane-header` (the --on-bg / --on-bg-muted / --on-bg-shadow overrides, position:relative, isolation:isolate) and the new `.lane-header::before` scrim rule entirely. Restore `.lane-title`'s original comment ("Lane headers sit on the wallpaper, not a surface — use luminance-derived on-background text so they stay legible against any background."). Restore `.lane-tab-count`'s `opacity: 0.85`.
2. meridian-extension/meridian.css: same revert, mirrored.
3. Leave components/SettingsPanel.js's applyOnBackground/global luminance logic as-is for now (not part of this revert) UNLESS your new approach below makes it dead code — if so, clean it up.
4. Remove/rewrite tests/laneHeaderContrast.test.mjs if it specifically asserts the scrim/backdrop-filter approach — replace with tests for the new approach below.

New approach requested instead: make the lane header text/icons literally INVERSE against whatever is directly behind them, using CSS mix-blend-mode (e.g. `mix-blend-mode: difference` or `exclusion` with `color: #fff` or similar base) on .lane-title, .lane-tab-count, .lane-delete-btn, and .lane-collapse-btn (and its icon/chevron). This auto-inverts per-pixel against the actual background color underneath with no JS luminance sampling and no scrim/backdrop — it should stay legible on any background, including the current default img/landscape.jpg gradient, without a visible bar.

Things to watch:
- mix-blend-mode needs correct stacking/isolation context so it blends against the page background (through any transparent ancestors) rather than against sibling elements — verify visually, don't just trust the property name.
- Check hover/focus states (.lane-title:hover, :focus) still look right — those currently switch to solid --text-primary/--surface for a "control" look; decide whether blend-mode should still apply on hover or whether the existing solid-surface hover state is fine to keep as is (probably keep hover/focus as-is, only change the resting/default state).
- Verify on both light and dark theme, against img/landscape.jpg specifically (the gradient case that started this), and against at least one solid/uniform background to make sure it doesn't regress.
- Run the full test suite and fix/replace any tests tied to the old scrim approach.

Reference: chat 99df29a9 in this repo has the full visual discussion, including image-3.png (original bug) and image-4.png (the scrim attempt that needs reverting).
label: Bug

activity.content:
Implemented the lane-header inverse-text treatment and removed the rejected scrim.

- Removed the full-width `.lane-header::before` backdrop, local token overrides, and isolated stacking context from both runtime stylesheets.
- Applied `color: #fff` plus `mix-blend-mode: difference` to resting titles, counts, delete controls, and collapse controls; the SVG chevron follows `currentColor`.
- Preserved surface-backed title focus/editable-hover, collapse-hover, and delete-hover states with normal blending.
- Restored the lane count to `opacity: 0.85`.
- Removed the now-unused global on-background luminance/token pipeline while retaining dominant-color accent analysis.
- Reworked lane-header coverage to assert direct inverse blending, absence of a scrim/isolation, chevron inheritance, and normal interactive-state blending.

Validation:
- Chromium visual checks passed on `img/landscape.jpg` in light and dark themes, plus near-black and near-white solid backgrounds; no header bar was present.
- Source/package CSS and SettingsPanel copies are byte-identical.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Full suite: **159 passed, 0 failed** via `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
